title.zh: 卷29 奚斤 叔孫建
title.raw: 卷29 奚斤 叔孫建 Volume 29: Xi Jin, Shu Sunjian

sentences.zh: 奚斤 叔孫建

translations.literal: Xi Jin; Shu Sun Jian
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin; Shu Sun Jian

sentences.zh: 奚斤，代人也，世典馬牧。

translations.literal: Xi Jin was a man of Dai; for generations his family superintended the horse herds.
translations.idiomatic: Xi Jin came from Dai. His line had for generations held charge of the imperial horse pastures.

sentences.zh: 父簞，有寵於昭成皇帝。

translations.literal: His father Dan enjoyed favor with Emperor Zhaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: His father Dan had won favor with Emperor Zhaocheng.

sentences.zh: 時國有良馬曰「騧騮」，一夜忽失，求之不得。

translations.literal: At the time the state had a fine horse called "Guamei"; one night it suddenly vanished, and though they searched it could not be found.
translations.idiomatic: The realm then had a fine horse called Guamei. One night it vanished without warning, and an exhaustive search failed to find it.

sentences.zh: 後知南部大人劉庫仁所盜，養於窟室。

translations.literal: Later it was learned that the southern-region chieftain Liu Kuren had stolen it and kept it in a cave dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: They later learned that Liu Kuren, chieftain of the southern region, had stolen it and was keeping it in a cave shelter.

sentences.zh: 簞聞而馳往取馬，庫仁以國甥恃寵，慚而逆擊簞。

translations.literal: Dan heard and raced to reclaim the horse; Kuren, as a kinsman of the imperial house relying on favor, was ashamed yet turned and attacked Dan.
translations.idiomatic: When Dan heard, he galloped off to recover the horse. Kuren, a royal kinsman who counted on imperial favor, was shamed—and struck back at Dan.

sentences.zh: 簞捽其髮落，傷其一乳。

translations.literal: Dan seized him and tore out his hair, wounding one breast.
translations.idiomatic: Dan seized him, tore out a handful of his hair, and injured one of his breasts.

sentences.zh: 及苻堅使庫仁與衞辰分領國部，簞懼，將家竄於民間。

translations.literal: When Fu Jian sent Kuren and Wei Chen to divide rule of the tribal divisions of the state, Dan was afraid and fled with his family among the common people.
translations.idiomatic: When Fu Jian sent Kuren and Wei Chen to divide leadership of the state's tribes, Dan grew afraid and hid his household among the people.

sentences.zh: 庫仁求之急，簞遂西奔衞辰。

translations.literal: Kuren pursued him hotly, so Dan fled west to Wei Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Kuren pressed the hunt hard, and Dan fled west to Wei Chen.

sentences.zh: 及太祖滅衞辰，簞晚乃得歸，故名位後於舊臣。

translations.literal: When Taizu destroyed Wei Chen, Dan only then returned late, so his rank and standing came after the older ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Taizu destroyed Wei Chen did Dan return—and late at that—so his rank and standing lagged behind the older ministers.

sentences.zh: 斤機敏，有識度。

translations.literal: Jin was quick-witted and had foresight and judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was quick-minded, with sound judgment and a keen eye for affairs.

sentences.zh: 登國初，與長孫肥等俱統禁兵。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Dengguo, together with Zhangsun Fei and others he commanded the forbidden troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Dengguo era he joined Zhangsun Fei and others in commanding the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 後以斤為侍郎，親近左右。

translations.literal: Later Jin was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and kept close at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was later made Attendant-in-Ordinary and kept near the throne.

sentences.zh: 從破慕容寶於參合。

translations.literal: He followed in defeating Murong Bao at Canhe.
translations.idiomatic: He marched when Murong Bao was broken at Canhe.

sentences.zh: 皇始初，從征中原，以斤為征東長史，拜越騎校尉，典宿衞禁旅。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Huangshi, he followed the campaign into the Central Plains; Jin was made Eastern Campaign Chief Clerk, appointed Colonel of Fast Cavalry, and put in charge of the palace guard and forbidden army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huangshi opened, he joined the drive into the Central Plains. Jin was made chief clerk on the eastern campaign, named Colonel of Fast Cavalry, and charged with the palace guard and forbidden troops.

sentences.zh: 車駕還京師，博陵、勃海、章武諸郡，羣盜並起，所在屯聚，拒害長吏。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the capital, bandits rose together in the commanderies of Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu, gathering everywhere and resisting and harming the chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial carriage returned to the capital, bandits rose together across Boling, Bohai, and Zhangwu, mustering wherever they could and killing or defying the local chiefs.

sentences.zh: 斤與略陽公元遵等率山東諸軍討平之。

translations.literal: Jin, together with Yuan Zun, Prince of Lueyang, and others led the armies east of the mountains to suppress and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin marched with Yuan Zun, Prince of Lueyang, and others at the head of the armies east of the mountains and put the revolt down.

sentences.zh: 從征高車諸部，大破之。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against the Gaoche tribes and defeated them greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He joined campaigns against the Gaoche tribes and broke them decisively.

sentences.zh: 又破厙狄、宥連部，徙其別部諸落於塞南。

translations.literal: He also defeated the Kudi and Youlian tribes and moved their separate tribes and clans south of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He also smashed the Kudi and Youlian and relocated their subsidiary tribes and clans south of the frontier.

sentences.zh: 又進擊侯莫陳部，俘虜獲雜畜十餘萬，至大峨谷，置戍而還。

translations.literal: He advanced again against the Houmochen tribe, captured prisoners and took more than a hundred thousand mixed livestock; reaching Da'e Valley, he set garrisons and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on against the Houmochen, he took captives and more than a hundred thousand head of mixed livestock, reached Da'e Valley, posted garrisons, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 遷都水使者，出為晉兵將軍，幽州刺史，賜爵山陽侯。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commissioner of the Waterways, sent out as General of Jin Troops and Governor of You Province, and granted the title Marquis of Shanyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved up to Commissioner of the Waterways, then sent out as General of Jin Troops and Governor of You Province, with the title Marquis of Shanyang.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，為鄭兵將軍，循行州郡，問民疾苦。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he became General of Zheng Troops, made circuit of the provinces and commanderies, and inquired into the people's hardships.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, Jin became General of Zheng Troops, toured the provinces and commanderies, and asked after the people's hardships.

sentences.zh: 章武民劉牙聚黨為亂，斤討平之。

translations.literal: Liu Ya of Zhangwu gathered a faction and rebelled; Jin campaigned and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ya of Zhangwu raised a faction in revolt; Jin campaigned against him and restored order.

sentences.zh: 詔以斤世忠孝，贈其父簞為長寧子。

translations.literal: An edict cited Jin's hereditary loyalty and filial piety and posthumously ennobled his father Dan as Viscount of Changning.
translations.idiomatic: An edict praised the loyalty and filial piety of Jin's line and posthumously ennobled his father Dan as Viscount of Changning.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸雲中，斤留守京師。

translations.literal: When Taizong visited Yunzhong, Jin remained to guard the capital.
translations.idiomatic: While Taizong was at Yunzhong, Jin stayed behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: 昌黎王慕容伯兒收合輕俠失志之徒李沈等三百餘人謀反，斤聞而召伯兒入天文殿東廡下，窮問款引，悉收其黨誅之。

translations.literal: Murong Bo'er, Prince of Changli, gathered more than three hundred men of restless spirit such as Li Shen and plotted rebellion; when Jin heard of it he summoned Bo'er into the eastern wing of the Astronomy Hall, questioned him until he confessed, and executed the whole faction.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Bo'er, Prince of Changli, rallied more than three hundred restless men, including Li Shen, in a plot to rebel. Jin heard of it, summoned Bo'er into the eastern wing of the Astronomy Hall, examined him until he confessed, and put the entire faction to death.

sentences.zh: 詔與南平公長孫嵩等俱坐朝堂，錄決囚徒。

translations.literal: He was ordered together with Zhangsun Song, Duke of Nanping, and others to sit in the court hall and record and decide criminal cases.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to sit in the court hall with Zhangsun Song, Duke of Nanping, and others to hear and decide criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 太宗大閱于東郊，治兵講武，以斤行左丞相。

translations.literal: Taizong held a great review at the eastern suburb, drilling troops and displaying arms; Jin acted as Left Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong held a grand review at the eastern suburb, drilling the army and displaying arms, with Jin serving as acting Left Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 大蒐於石會山。

translations.literal: A great hunt was held at Stone Assembly Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: A great hunt was held at Stone Assembly Mountain.

sentences.zh: 車駕西巡，詔斤為先驅，討越勒部於鹿那山，[1]大破之，獲馬五萬匹，牛羊二十萬頭，徙二萬餘家而還。

translations.literal: On the western tour, Jin was ordered as vanguard to attack the Yuele tribe at Lüna Mountain; he defeated them greatly, took fifty thousand horses and two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, moved more than twenty thousand households, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: On the western tour Jin was sent ahead to strike the Yuele at Lüna Mountain. He routed them, took fifty thousand horses and two hundred thousand cattle and sheep, resettled more than twenty thousand households, and returned.

sentences.zh: 又詔斤與長孫嵩等八人，坐止車門右，聽理萬機。

translations.literal: Again Jin and eight others including Zhangsun Song were ordered to sit to the right of the Halting Carriage Gate and handle the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Jin and eight others, including Zhangsun Song, were again ordered to sit to the right of the Halting Carriage Gate and attend to the myriad affairs of state.

sentences.zh: 蠕蠕犯塞，令斤等追之。

translations.literal: The Rouran raided the border; Jin and others were ordered to pursue.
translations.idiomatic: When the Rouran raided the frontier, Jin and others were sent in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 事具蠕蠕傳。

translations.literal: The matter is fully recorded in the Rouran biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the Rouran biography.

sentences.zh: 拜天部大人，進爵為公，命斤出入乘軺軒，備威儀導從。

translations.literal: He was appointed Grandee of the Heavenly Division, advanced in rank to duke, and ordered to ride in a light carriage when entering and leaving, with full insignia and escort.
translations.idiomatic: He was named Grandee of the Heavenly Division, raised to duke, and ordered to travel in a light carriage with full insignia and an escort whenever he entered or left court.

sentences.zh: 世祖之為皇太子，臨朝聽政，以斤為左輔。

translations.literal: When Shizu was crown prince and presided at court, Jin was made his left assistant.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu was crown prince and held court, Jin was made his left assistant.

sentences.zh: 劉義符立，其大臣不附，國內離阻。

translations.literal: When Liu Yifu was enthroned, his great ministers were not loyal and the state was divided within.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yifu took the throne, his senior ministers would not rally to him and the realm split within.

sentences.zh: 乃遣斤收劉裕前侵河南地，假斤節，都督前鋒諸軍事、司空公、晉兵大將軍、行揚州刺史，率吳兵將軍公孫表等南征。

translations.literal: They then sent Jin to recover the Henan territory Liu Yu had earlier seized; he was given credentials, made Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, Minister of Works, Great General of Jin Troops, and acting Governor of Yang Province, and led a southern campaign with Gongsun Biao, General of Wu Troops, and others.
translations.idiomatic: Wei then sent Jin to recover the Henan lands Liu Yu had taken earlier. He was given the imperial baton as commander of the vanguard, Minister of Works, Great General of Jin Troops, and acting Governor of Yang Province, and marched south with Gongsun Biao, General of Wu Troops, and others.

sentences.zh: 用表計攻滑臺，不拔，求濟師。

translations.literal: Using Biao's plan they attacked Huatai but could not take it and requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Following Biao's plan they attacked Huatai but failed to take it and asked for more troops.

sentences.zh: 太宗怒其不先略地，切責之。

translations.literal: Taizong was angry they had not first seized territory and sternly rebuked them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was furious that they had not seized ground first and rebuked them sharply.

sentences.zh: 乃親南巡，次中山。

translations.literal: He then personally toured south and halted at Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: He then led a southern tour in person and stopped at Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 義符東郡太守王景度捐城遁走，司馬楚之等並遣使詣斤降。

translations.literal: Yifu's Administrator of Dongjun Wang Jingdu abandoned the city and fled; Chu Zhi the Administrator of Staff and others all sent envoys to Jin to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jingdu, Yifu's administrator of Dongjun, abandoned his city and fled. Chu Zhi and other senior officers all sent envoys to Jin to surrender.

sentences.zh: 斤自滑臺趣洛陽，義符虎牢守將毛德祖遣其司馬翟廣、將軍姚勇錯、竇霸等率五千人據土樓以拒斤，斤進擊，破之。

translations.literal: Jin left Huatai and pressed on toward Luoyang; Dezu, defender of Hulao, sent his Administrator of Staff Zhai Guang, Generals Yao Yongcuo, Dou Ba, and others with five thousand men to hold an earthen tower and resist Jin, who attacked and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Jin marched from Huatai toward Luoyang. Mao Dezu, defender of Hulao, sent his chief clerk Zhai Guang and the generals Yao Yongcuo and Dou Ba with five thousand men to hold an earthen tower against him; Jin attacked and routed them.

sentences.zh: 廣等單馬走免，盡殪其眾。

translations.literal: Guang and the others escaped alone on horseback; their entire force was slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Guang and the others fled alone on horseback; their whole force was wiped out.

sentences.zh: 斤長驅至虎牢，軍於汜東。

translations.literal: Jin drove swiftly to Hulao and encamped east of the Si.
translations.idiomatic: Jin drove hard to Hulao and pitched camp east of the Si.

sentences.zh: 留表守輜重，自率輕兵徇下河南、穎川、陳郡以南，百姓無不歸附。

translations.literal: He left Biao to guard the baggage train and personally led light troops to overrun the region south of Henan, Yingchuan, and Chen commanderies; none of the common people failed to submit.
translations.idiomatic: He left Biao with the baggage train and himself led light troops through the lands south of Henan, Yingchuan, and Chen; the people submitted everywhere he went.

sentences.zh: 義符陳留太守嚴稜以郡降。

translations.literal: Yifu's Administrator of Chenliu Yan Ling surrendered the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's Ling, Yifu's administrator of Chenliu, surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 斤遂平兗豫諸郡，還圍虎牢。

translations.literal: Jin then pacified the commanderies of Yan and Yu and returned to besiege Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: Jin then pacified the commanderies of Yan and Yu and returned to lay siege to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 德祖拒守不下。

translations.literal: Dezu held out and could not be taken down.
translations.idiomatic: Dezu held the city and would not yield.

sentences.zh: 及虎牢潰，斤置守宰以撫之。

translations.literal: When Hulao fell, Jin set guards and administrators to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: When Hulao fell, Jin posted guards and local administrators to settle the region.

sentences.zh: 自魏初，大將行師，唯長孫嵩拒劉裕，斤征河南，獨給漏刻及十二牙旗。

translations.literal: Since the beginning of Wei, when great generals took the field, only Zhangsun Song opposing Liu Yu and Jin campaigning in Henan were alone granted clepsydrae and twelve tusked banners.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Wei, of all great generals who took the field, only Zhangsun Song against Liu Yu and Jin in Henan were given clepsydrae and twelve tusked banners.

sentences.zh: 太宗崩，斤乃班師。

translations.literal: When Taizong died, Jin withdrew the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong died, Jin led the army home.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，進爵宜城王，仍為司空。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, Jin was advanced to Prince of Yicheng and remained Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu came to the throne, Jin was raised to Prince of Yicheng and kept his post as Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 世祖征赫連昌，遣斤率義兵將軍封禮等督四萬五千人襲蒲坂。

translations.literal: When Shizu campaigned against Helian Chang, he sent Jin with General of Righteous Troops Feng Li and others to command forty-five thousand men in a surprise attack on Puban.
translations.idiomatic: As Shizu marched against Helian Chang, he sent Jin with Feng Li, General of Righteous Troops, and others to lead forty-five thousand men in a surprise strike on Puban.

sentences.zh: 昌守將赫連乙升聞斤將至，遣使告昌。

translations.literal: Chang's defender Helian Yisheng, hearing Jin was coming, sent a messenger to report to Chang.
translations.idiomatic: Helian Yisheng, Chang's garrison commander, heard Jin was approaching and sent a messenger to warn Chang.

sentences.zh: 使至統萬，見大軍已圍其城，還告乙升曰：「昌已敗矣。

translations.literal: When the messenger reached Tongwan, he saw the great army already besieging the city; returning he told Yisheng, "Chang is already defeated."
translations.idiomatic: The messenger reached Tongwan, saw the main force already besieging the city, and on his return told Yisheng, "Chang is already lost."

sentences.zh: 」乙升懼，棄蒲坂西走。

translations.literal: Yisheng was afraid and abandoned Puban, fleeing west.
translations.idiomatic: Yisheng took fright, abandoned Puban, and fled west.

sentences.zh: 斤追敗之，乙升遂奔長安。

translations.literal: Jin pursued and defeated him; Yisheng then fled to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pursued, defeated him, and Yisheng fled on to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 斤入蒲坂，收其資器，百姓安業。

translations.literal: Jin entered Puban, collected its stores and equipment, and the people settled in their occupations.
translations.idiomatic: Jin entered Puban, gathered its stores and gear, and the people returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 昌弟助興，先守長安，乙升至，復與助興棄長安，西走安定，斤又西據長安。

translations.literal: Chang's younger brother Zhuxing had earlier held Chang'an; when Yisheng arrived he again abandoned Chang'an with Zhuxing and fled west to Anding, and Jin again seized Chang'an in the west.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's brother Zhuxing had been holding Chang'an. When Yisheng arrived, he and Zhuxing again abandoned the city and fled west to Anding, and Jin took Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 於是秦雍氐羌皆來歸附。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong all came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Then the Di and Qiang of Qin and Yong came over in submission.

sentences.zh: 與赫連定相持，累戰破定。

translations.literal: He held Changding in stalemate and in repeated battles defeated Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He locked horns with Helian Ding and beat him again and again in battle.

sentences.zh: 定聞昌敗，遂走上邽，斤追之，至雍，不及而還。

translations.literal: When Ding heard Chang had been defeated, he fled up to Shanggui; Jin pursued to Yong but could not catch him and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding heard Chang was lost, he fled toward Shanggui. Jin chased as far as Yong, failed to overtake him, and turned back.

sentences.zh: 詔斤班師，斤上疏曰：「赫連昌亡保上邽，鳩合餘燼，未有盤據之資。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Jin to withdraw; Jin memorialized, "Helian Chang, a fugitive from a ruined state, is gathering the last embers of his house and has no footing from which to hold ground."
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to withdraw, Jin memorialized: "Helian Chang, a fugitive from a ruined realm, is rallying the last embers of his house and has no footing left to hold."

sentences.zh: 今因其危，滅之為易。

translations.literal: Now that he is in peril, destroying him would be easy.
translations.idiomatic: Strike him in this moment of peril and his destruction will be easy.

sentences.zh: 請益鎧馬，平昌而還。

translations.literal: I ask for more armor and horses to pacify Chang and then return.
translations.idiomatic: Grant me more armor and horses to finish Chang and then I will return.

sentences.zh: 」世祖曰：「昌亡國叛夫，擊之勞傷將士，且可息兵，取之不晚。

translations.literal: Shizu said, "Chang is a rebel who has lost his state; striking him would weary the officers and soldiers. For now let the army rest—the capture can wait."
translations.idiomatic: Shizu replied, "Chang is a rebel who has lost his state. Attacking him would only weary the troops. Rest the army for now; he can be taken later."

sentences.zh: 」斤抗表固執，乃許之，給斤萬人，遣將軍劉拔送馬三千匹與斤。

translations.literal: Jin submitted a memorial insisting; only then was he permitted, given ten thousand men, and General Liu Ba was sent with three thousand horses to Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pressed his case in a further memorial until Shizu relented, gave him ten thousand men, and sent General Liu Ba with three thousand horses to join him.

sentences.zh: 斤進討安定，昌退保平涼。

translations.literal: Jin advanced against Anding; Chang withdrew to hold Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Jin pressed on toward Anding; Chang fell back to defend Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 斤屯軍安定，以糧竭馬死，遂深壘自固。

translations.literal: Jin encamped at Anding; grain ran out and horses died, so he dug in behind deep ramparts.
translations.idiomatic: Jin camped at Anding, but as grain gave out and horses died he dug in behind deep fortifications.

sentences.zh: 監軍侍御史安頡擊昌，擒之。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretary An Gu attacked Chang and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretary An Gu attacked Chang and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 語在頡傳。

translations.literal: The account is in An Gu's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in An Gu's biography.

sentences.zh: 昌眾復立昌弟定為主，守平涼。

translations.literal: Chang's followers again set up Chang's younger brother Ding as ruler and held Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Chang's followers raised his brother Ding and held Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 斤自以元帥，而擒昌之功，更不在己，深耻之。

translations.literal: Jin, as supreme commander, felt deep shame that the merit of capturing Chang was not his.
translations.idiomatic: As supreme commander, Jin was deeply shamed that the credit for capturing Chang had gone to another.

sentences.zh: 乃舍輜重，輕齎三日糧，追定於平涼。

translations.literal: He abandoned the baggage train, took only three days' rations on light march, and pursued Ding to Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: He cast off his baggage, marched light with only three days' grain, and chased Ding to Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 娥清欲尋水而往，斤不從，自北道邀其走路。

translations.literal: E Qing wished to go by way of the water, but Jin would not follow and instead blocked Ding's route of escape from the north.
translations.idiomatic: E Qing wanted to follow the watercourse, but Jin refused and instead barred Ding's escape route from the north.

sentences.zh: 定眾將出，會一小將有罪亡入賊，具告其實。

translations.literal: As Ding's force was about to march out, a junior officer who had committed a crime fled into the enemy camp and told them everything.
translations.idiomatic: Just as Ding's army was preparing to move out, a junior officer guilty of an offense fled to the enemy and told them the whole truth.

sentences.zh: 定知斤軍無糧乏水，乃邀斤前後。

translations.literal: Ding learned Jin's army lacked grain and water and intercepted Jin from front and rear.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Jin's troops were short of grain and water, Ding struck him from before and behind.

sentences.zh: 斤眾大潰，斤及娥清、劉拔為定所擒，士卒死者六七千人。

translations.literal: Jin's army collapsed in great defeat; Jin, E Qing, and Liu Ba were captured by Ding, and six or seven thousand soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's army broke in utter rout. Jin, E Qing, and Liu Ba were taken by Ding, and six or seven thousand soldiers died.

sentences.zh: 後世祖克平涼，斤等得歸。

translations.literal: Later, when Shizu took Pingliang, Jin and the others were released and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when Shizu took Pingliang, Jin and the others were freed and returned.

sentences.zh: 免為宰人，使負酒食從駕還京師以辱之。

translations.literal: He was reduced to palace steward and made to carry wine and food in the train back to the capital as a humiliation.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to palace steward and made to carry wine and food in the imperial train back to the capital—a public humiliation.

sentences.zh: 尋拜安東將軍，降爵為公。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed General Who Pacifies the East and demoted in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was named General Who Pacifies the East and reduced in rank to duke.

sentences.zh: 車駕將討馮文通，詔斤發幽州民及密雲丁零萬餘人，運攻具出南道。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage was about to campaign against Feng Wentong, Jin was ordered to mobilize the people of You Province and more than ten thousand Dingling of Miyun to transport siege engines by the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to campaign against Feng Wentong, Jin was ordered to raise the people of You Province and more than ten thousand Miyun Dingling to haul siege engines along the southern route.

sentences.zh: 太延初，為衞尉，改為弘農王，[2]加征南大將軍。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Taiyan he was made Commandant of the Guards, changed to Prince of Hongnong, and additionally named Great General Who Conquers the South.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Taiyan he became Commandant of the Guards, was made Prince of Hongnong, and additionally named Great General Who Conquers the South.

sentences.zh: 後為萬騎大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Great General of Ten Thousand Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He later became Great General of Ten Thousand Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 世祖大集羣臣於西堂，議伐涼州。

translations.literal: Shizu gathered the ministers in the Western Hall to deliberate on a campaign against Liang Province.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu assembled his ministers in the Western Hall to debate an expedition against Liang Province.

sentences.zh: 斤等三十餘人議曰：「河西王牧犍，西垂下國，雖內不純臣，而外修職貢，宜加寬宥，恕其微愆。

translations.literal: Jin and more than thirty others submitted, "Mujian, King of Hexi, is a petty state on the western marches. Though inwardly no pure subject, outwardly he still pays tribute and duty; he should be treated with leniency and his small faults forgiven."
translations.idiomatic: Jin and more than thirty others argued: "Mujian of Hexi is a petty western state. Though not a loyal subject at heart, he still pays tribute and duty outwardly; he should be shown leniency and his small faults overlooked."

sentences.zh: 去歲新征，士馬疲弊，未可大舉，宜且覊縻。

translations.literal: Last year's new campaign has worn out men and horses; a great expedition is not yet possible—we should keep him on a loose rein for now.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign just past has exhausted men and horses; a major expedition is not yet possible, and he should be held on a loose rein.

sentences.zh: 其地鹵薄，略無水草，大軍既到，不得久停。

translations.literal: The land is briny and thin, with hardly any grass or water; once the great army arrives it cannot stay long.
translations.idiomatic: The country is salt-poor and barren, with scarcely grass or water; a great army cannot linger once it arrives.

sentences.zh: 彼聞軍來，必嬰城固守。

translations.literal: When they hear the army is coming they are sure to cling to their walls and hold fast.
translations.idiomatic: When they hear our army is coming, they will surely cling to their walls.

sentences.zh: 攻則難拔，野無所掠，終無克獲。

translations.literal: If we attack it will be hard to take; in the open country there is nothing to seize, and in the end nothing will be gained.
translations.idiomatic: An assault will be hard to finish, and with nothing to forage in the field we will gain nothing in the end."

sentences.zh: 」世祖不從，征之。

translations.literal: Shizu did not follow this and campaigned.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu would not listen and marched to war.

sentences.zh: 涼州平，以戰功賜僮隸七十戶。

translations.literal: When Liang Province was pacified, for battle merit he was granted seventy households of bond servants.
translations.idiomatic: When Liang Province was pacified, he was rewarded with seventy households of bond servants for his service in the field.

sentences.zh: 以斤元老，賜安車，平決刑獄，諮訪朝政。

translations.literal: As an elder statesman he was granted a comfort carriage, authority to decide criminal cases, and consultation on court governance.
translations.idiomatic: As a senior minister he was given a comfort carriage, authority to decide criminal cases, and a voice in court governance.

sentences.zh: 斤聰辯強識，善於談論，遠說先朝故事，雖未皆是，時有所得。

translations.literal: Jin was clever in debate and had a strong memory; skilled in discussion, when he spoke at length of former dynasties' affairs, though not all was correct, he sometimes hit the mark.
translations.idiomatic: Jin was sharp in debate and retentive in memory. In discussion he would range over the affairs of earlier dynasties; though not always right, he often struck home.

sentences.zh: 聽者歎美之。

translations.literal: Listeners sighed and praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard him sighed in admiration.

sentences.zh: 每議大政，多見從用，朝廷稱焉。

translations.literal: Whenever great policy was debated, his views were often adopted, and the court spoke well of him.
translations.idiomatic: On great matters of state his counsel was often taken, and the court spoke well of him.

sentences.zh: 真君九年薨，時年八十。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenjun he died, aged eighty.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year of Zhenjun, at the age of eighty.

sentences.zh: 世祖親臨哀慟，諡曰昭王。

translations.literal: Shizu came in person to mourn and wept; he was given the posthumous title Prince Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu came in person to mourn and weep. He was posthumously titled Prince Zhao.

sentences.zh: 斤有數十婦，子男二十餘人。

translations.literal: Jin had several tens of wives and more than twenty sons.
translations.idiomatic: Jin had several dozen wives and more than twenty sons.

sentences.zh: 長子他觀襲爵。

translations.literal: His eldest son Taguan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Taguan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 世祖曰：「斤關西之敗，國有常刑。

translations.literal: Shizu said, "Jin's defeat west of the passes carries the state's fixed penalty.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu said, "Jin's defeat in the west carried the state's fixed penalty.

sentences.zh: 以其佐命先朝，故復其爵秩，將收孟明之效。

translations.literal: Because he had aided the founding of the dynasty in the former reign, his rank and title were restored, that he might achieve the effect of Meng Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Because he had aided the founding in the previous reign, his rank and title were restored—the court hoped he would yet earn the redemption Meng Ming won.

sentences.zh: 今斤終其天年，君臣之分全矣。

translations.literal: Now Jin has ended his natural span of years, and the bond between ruler and minister is complete."
translations.idiomatic: Now Jin has lived out his years, and the bond between ruler and minister stands whole."

sentences.zh: 」於是降他觀爵為公，除廣平太守。

translations.literal: Thereupon Taguan's title was reduced to duke and he was made Administrator of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: Taguan's title was lowered to duke and he was appointed Administrator of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 後為都將，征懸瓠，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Later he became Chief Commander, campaigned against Xuanchi, and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as chief commander, marched against Xuanchi, and died on campaign.

sentences.zh: 子延，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Yan inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 出為瓦城鎮將。

translations.literal: He was sent out as garrison commander of Wacheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as garrison commander of Wacheng.

translations.literal: [3] He died.
translations.idiomatic: [3] He died.

sentences.zh: 子緒，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Xu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 初為散令，後為太中大夫，加左將軍。

translations.literal: At first he was a Master of Scattered Affairs; later he became Grand Master of Palace Counsel and was additionally named General of the Left.
translations.idiomatic: He began as Master of Scattered Affairs, then became Grand Master of Palace Counsel with the additional title General of the Left.

sentences.zh: 開建五等，封弘農郡開國侯，食邑三百戶。

translations.literal: When the five ranks were established, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of a Hongnong commandery state with three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When the five ranks were instituted, he was enfeoffed as Marquis of a Hongnong commandery state with three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 後例降為縣，改封澄城縣開國侯，增邑九百戶。

translations.literal: Later by precedent he was reduced to county rank, changed to Marquis of a Chengcheng county state, and his fief was increased by nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: By later precedent he was reduced to county rank, made Marquis of a Chengcheng county state, and his fief rose by nine hundred households.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子遵，襲封。

translations.literal: His son Zun inherited the fief.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zun inherited the fief.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈鎮遠將軍、洛州刺史，諡曰哀侯。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously given General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Luo Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Ai.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously named General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Luo Province, with the posthumous title Marquis Ai.

sentences.zh: 無子，國除。

translations.literal: He had no son, and the fief was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: He left no son, and the fief was abolished.

sentences.zh: 太和中，高祖追錄先朝功臣，以斤配食廟庭。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era, Gaozu recorded the merits of former-dynasty ministers and granted Jin a place in the temple sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In Taihe, Gaozu recorded the merits of ministers of the founding reign and granted Jin a place in the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 世宗繼絕世，詔以緒弟子鑒特紹其後，以承封邑。

translations.literal: Shizong continued a line that had ended; an edict made Xu's nephew Jian specially succeed him to receive the fief.
translations.idiomatic: When the line was about to die out, Shizong ordered Xu's nephew Jian to succeed specially and hold the fief.

sentences.zh: 鑒卒於中堅將軍、司徒從事中郎。

translations.literal: Jian died as General of the Palace Attendants and Attendant of the Masters of Writing in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Jian died while serving as General of the Palace Attendants and Attendant of the Masters of Writing in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 贈龍驤將軍、肆州刺史。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given General of Dragon Agility and Governor of Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named General of Dragon Agility and Governor of Si Province.

sentences.zh: 子紹宗，武定中，開府田曹參軍。

translations.literal: His son Shaozong, in the Wuding era, was an aide in the Bureau of Fields in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shaozong, in the Wuding era, served as an aide in the Bureau of Fields of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 他觀弟和觀，太祖時內侍左右。

translations.literal: Taguan's younger brother He Guan, in Taizu's time, attended at the ruler's side within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He Guan, Taguan's younger brother, attended Taizu within the palace.

sentences.zh: 太宗以其世典戎御，遂拜典御都尉，賜爵廣興子，建威將軍。

translations.literal: Taizong, because his family for generations had superintended military equipage, appointed him Commandant of the Palace Equipage, granted the title Viscount of Guangxing, and named him General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, noting that his line had for generations managed the imperial equipage, made him Commandant of the Palace Equipage, granted him Viscount of Guangxing, and named him General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 尋進為宜陽侯，加龍驤將軍，領牧官中郎將。

translations.literal: Soon he was advanced to Marquis of Yiyang, additionally named General of Dragon Agility, and put in charge as Colonel of the Herds Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon raised to Marquis of Yiyang, given the additional title General of Dragon Agility, and made Colonel of the Herds Office.

sentences.zh: 出為冀青二州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Ji and Qing provinces.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Ji and Qing provinces.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 子冀州，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Jizhou inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jizhou inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 冀州弟受真，為中散。

translations.literal: Jizhou's younger brother Shouzhen was a Master of Scattered Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Jizhou's younger brother Shouzhen served as Master of Scattered Affairs.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，拜龍驤將軍，賜爵成都侯。

translations.literal: When Gaozong took the throne, he was appointed General of Dragon Agility and granted the title Marquis of Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozong came to the throne, he was named General of Dragon Agility and granted the title Marquis of Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，出為離石鎮將。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Within the Palace and sent out as garrison commander of Lishi.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to Attendant Within the Palace, then posted as garrison commander of Lishi.

sentences.zh: 和觀弟拔，太宗時內侍左右。

translations.literal: He Guan's younger brother Ba, in Taizong's time, attended at the ruler's side within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Ba, He Guan's younger brother, attended Taizong within the palace.

sentences.zh: 世祖即位，稍遷侍中、選部尚書、鎮南將軍，賜爵樂陵公。

translations.literal: When Shizu took the throne, he was gradually advanced to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Bureau of Selection, General Who Guards the South, and granted the title Duke of Leling.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu came to the throne, he rose step by step to Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of the Bureau of Selection, General Who Guards the South, and Duke of Leling.

sentences.zh: 後以罪徙邊。

translations.literal: Later for a crime he was banished to the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: He was later banished to the frontier for a crime.

sentences.zh: 徵為散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕，戰沒。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against the Rouran and died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: He marched against the Rouran and fell in battle.

sentences.zh: 子買奴，有寵於顯祖，官至神部長。

translations.literal: His son Mainu enjoyed favor with Xianzu and reached the post of Chief of the Divine Division.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mainu won favor with Xianzu and rose to chief of the Divine Division.

sentences.zh: 與安成王萬安國不平，安國矯詔殺買奴於苑內。

translations.literal: He was at odds with Wan Anguo, Prince of Ancheng; Anguo forged an edict and killed Mainu in the park.
translations.idiomatic: He quarreled with Wan Anguo, Prince of Ancheng, who forged an edict and killed Mainu in the imperial park.

sentences.zh: 高祖賜安國死，追贈買奴為并州刺史、新興公。

translations.literal: Gaozu sentenced Anguo to death and posthumously ennobled Mainu as Governor of Bing Province and Duke of Xinxing.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu put Anguo to death and posthumously ennobled Mainu as Governor of Bing Province and Duke of Xinxing.

sentences.zh: 斤弟普回，陽曲護軍。

translations.literal: Jin's younger brother Puhui was Protector of the Army of Yangqu.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's younger brother Puhui was Protector of the Army of Yangqu.

sentences.zh: 普回子烏侯，世祖時拜治書御史，建義將軍，賜爵夷餘侯。

translations.literal: Puhui's son Wuhou, in Shizu's time, was appointed Imperial Censor, General Who Establishes Righteousness, and granted the title Marquis of Yiyu.
translations.idiomatic: Puhui's son Wuhou, under Shizu, became Imperial Censor and General Who Establishes Righteousness, with the title Marquis of Yiyu.

sentences.zh: 從征蠕蠕及赫連昌，以功進爵城陽公，加員外散騎常侍，出為虎牢鎮將。

translations.literal: He followed campaigns against the Rouran and Helian Chang; for merit he was advanced to Duke of Chengyang, additionally named Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and sent out as garrison commander of Hulao.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Rouran and Helian Chang, was raised to Duke of Chengyang for his service, given the additional title Supernumerary Regular Attendant of Scattered Cavalry, and posted to Hulao.

sentences.zh: 興光中卒，喪禮依其伯父弘農王故事。

translations.literal: He died in the Xingguang era; funeral rites followed the precedent of his uncle the Prince of Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xingguang; his funeral followed the precedent set for his uncle the Prince of Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He was buried by accompaniment at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried by accompaniment at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 烏侯子兠，世祖時親侍左右，隨從征討，常持御劍。

translations.literal: Wuhou's son Dou, in Shizu's time, attended close at the ruler's side and followed in campaigns, often bearing the imperial sword.
translations.idiomatic: Dou, Wuhou's son, attended Shizu in person on campaign and often carried the imperial sword.

sentences.zh: 後以罪徙龍城。

translations.literal: Later for a crime he was banished to Longcheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was later banished to Longcheng for a crime.

sentences.zh: 尋徵為知臣監。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Supervisor of Knowing Subjects.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Supervisor of Knowing Subjects.

sentences.zh: 出為薄骨律鎮將，假鎮遠將軍，賜爵富城侯。

translations.literal: He was sent out as garrison commander of Boguli, acting General Who Pacifies the Distance, and granted the title Marquis of Fucheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted to Boguli as garrison commander, acting General Who Pacifies the Distance, with the title Marquis of Fucheng.

sentences.zh: 時高車叛，圍鎮城。

translations.literal: At the time the Gaoche rebelled and besieged the garrison town.
translations.idiomatic: The Gaoche rebelled then and besieged the town.

sentences.zh: 兠擊破之，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: Dou attacked and defeated them, taking more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: Dou broke the siege and took more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 延興中卒。

translations.literal: He died in the Yansing era.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Yansing.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建，代人也。

translations.literal: Shu Sun Jian was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Sun Jian came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 父骨，為昭成母王太后所養，與皇子同列。

translations.literal: His father Gu was raised by Empress Dowager Wang, mother of Zhaocheng, and ranked with the imperial princes.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gu was raised by Empress Dowager Wang, mother of Emperor Zhaocheng, and stood in the same rank as the imperial princes.

sentences.zh: 建少以智勇著稱。

translations.literal: Jian in youth was famed for wisdom and courage.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Jian was known for wisdom and courage.

sentences.zh: 太祖之幸賀蘭部，建常從左右。

translations.literal: When Taizu visited the Helan tribe, Jian often followed at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu visited the Helan, Jian was often at his side.

sentences.zh: 登國初，以建為外朝大人，與安同等十三人迭典庶事，參軍國之謀。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dengguo, Jian was made outer-court grandee; with An Tong and twelve others he took turns overseeing common affairs and joined in the state's counsels.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of Dengguo he was made outer-court grandee; with An Tong and twelve others he took turns in daily governance and joined the realm's counsels.

sentences.zh: 隨秦王觚使慕容垂，歷六載乃還。

translations.literal: He followed Prince Gu of Qin as envoy to Murong Chui and was away six years before returning.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Prince Gu of Qin as envoy to Murong Chui and was gone six years before he returned.

sentences.zh: 拜後將軍。

translations.literal: He was appointed General of the Rear.
translations.idiomatic: He was named General of the Rear.

sentences.zh: 頃之，為都水使者，中領軍，賜爵安平公，加龍驤將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he became Commissioner of the Waterways, Central Army Commander, was granted the title Duke of Anping, and additionally named General of Dragon Agility.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he became Commissioner of the Waterways and Central Army Commander, was made Duke of Anping, and given the additional title General of Dragon Agility.

sentences.zh: 出為并州刺史。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Governor of Bing Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Governor of Bing Province.

sentences.zh: 後以公事免，守鄴城園。

translations.literal: Later he was dismissed for public business and guarded the park at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: He was later dismissed over public business and kept guard over the park at Ye.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，念建前功，乃以建為正直將軍，相州刺史。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, mindful of Jian's earlier merit, he made Jian General of Uprightness and Governor of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, remembering Jian's earlier service, he made him General of Uprightness and Governor of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 飢胡劉虎等聚黨反叛，公孫表等為虎所敗。

translations.literal: The famished Hu Liu Hu and others gathered factions and rebelled; Gongsun Biao and others were defeated by Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hu of the famished Hu and others raised factions in revolt; Gongsun Biao and others were beaten by Hu.

sentences.zh: 太宗假建前號安平公，督表等以討虎，斬首萬餘級。

translations.literal: Taizong lent Jian his former title Duke of Anping and had him command Biao and others to campaign against Hu; more than ten thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong restored Jian's former title Duke of Anping and set him over Biao and others against Hu; they took more than ten thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 餘眾奔走，投沁而死，水為不流，虜其眾十萬餘口。

translations.literal: The remainder fled in panic, threw themselves into the Qin River and drowned, and the water ceased to flow; more than a hundred thousand of the enemy were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors fled in panic, threw themselves into the Qin, and drowned until the water would not flow; more than a hundred thousand were taken.

sentences.zh: 司馬德宗將劉裕伐姚泓，令其部將王仲德為前鋒，將逼滑臺。

translations.literal: Sima Dezong was about to send Liu Yu to campaign against Yao Hong; he ordered his subordinate general Wang Zhongde as vanguard, who was about to press on Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Dezong was sending Liu Yu against Yao Hong and put Wang Zhongde in the vanguard to press toward Huatai.

sentences.zh: 兗州刺史尉建率所部棄城濟河，仲德遂入滑臺。

translations.literal: Governor of Yan Province Wei Jian led his command and abandoned the city to cross the river; Zhongde then entered Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Jian, Governor of Yan, abandoned his city and crossed the river; Zhongde marched into Huatai.

sentences.zh: 乃宣言曰：「晉本意欲以布帛七萬匹假道於魏，不謂魏之守將便爾棄城。

translations.literal: He then proclaimed, "The Jin originally meant to borrow passage through Wei with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk, and did not expect Wei's defending general to abandon the city so readily."
translations.idiomatic: He proclaimed: "Jin meant only to borrow passage through Wei with seventy thousand bolts of cloth and silk—they never expected Wei's commander to throw the city away."

sentences.zh: 」太宗聞之，詔建自河內向枋頭以觀其勢。

translations.literal: When Taizong heard of it, he ordered Jian from Henei toward Fangtou to observe their strength.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong heard and ordered Jian from Henei toward Fangtou to gauge their strength.

sentences.zh: 仲德入滑臺月餘，又詔建渡河曜威，斬尉建，投其屍於河。

translations.literal: More than a month after Zhongde entered Huatai, Jian was again ordered to cross the river and display might; he executed Wei Jian and cast his corpse into the river.
translations.idiomatic: A month after Zhongde took Huatai, Jian was ordered to cross the river in a show of force, execute Wei Jian, and cast his body into the river.

sentences.zh: 呼仲德軍人與語，詰其侵境之意。

translations.literal: He called out to Zhongde's soldiers and spoke with them, questioning their intent in invading the border.
translations.idiomatic: He hailed Zhongde's men and questioned their purpose in crossing the border.

sentences.zh: 仲德遣司馬竺和之，建命公孫表與言。

translations.literal: Zhongde sent his Administrator of Staff Zhu Hezhi; Jian ordered Gongsun Biao to speak with him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde sent his chief clerk Zhu Hezhi; Jian had Gongsun Biao answer him.

sentences.zh: 和之曰：「王征虜為劉太尉所遣，入河西行，將取洛城，掃山陵之寇，非敢侵犯魏境。

translations.literal: Hezhi said, "The Campaigning King was sent by Grand Marshal Liu into the Hexi route to take Luoyang and sweep away the raiders of the imperial tombs; he does not dare invade Wei's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi said, "The Campaigning King was sent by Grand Marshal Liu along the Hexi route to take Luoyang and clear the tombs of raiders—not to invade Wei."

sentences.zh: 太尉自遣使請魏帝，陳將假道。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal himself sent envoys to request passage of the Wei emperor and stated his wish to borrow the road.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal himself has sent envoys to the Wei emperor to ask for passage.

sentences.zh: 而魏兗州刺史不相體解，望風捐去，因空城而入，非戰攻相逼也。

translations.literal: The Wei Governor of Yan did not understand one another's intent and fled at the sight of the wind, so they entered an empty city; it was not that attack and coercion forced them.
translations.idiomatic: Your Governor of Yan misunderstood us and fled, so they walked into an empty city—this was no assault under arms.

sentences.zh: 魏晉和好之義不廢於前。

translations.literal: The meaning of Jin-Wei friendship is not abandoned from before.
translations.idiomatic: The friendship of Jin and Wei still stands from before.

sentences.zh: 」表曰：「尉建失守之罪，自有常刑，將更遣良牧。

translations.literal: Biao said, "Wei Jian's crime of losing his post has its fixed penalty; a better governor will be sent again. Your army should go west, or you will let a small matter overturn the body of friendly relations."
translations.idiomatic: Biao said, "Wei Jian's failure carries its fixed penalty; a better governor will replace him. Your army should march west, or a small matter will overturn our friendship."

sentences.zh: 彼軍宜西，不然將以小致大乖和好之體。

translations.literal: Your army should go west, or you will let a small matter overturn the body of friendly relations.
translations.idiomatic: March west, or a small matter will overturn the body of our friendship.

sentences.zh: 」和之曰：「王征虜權住於此，以待眾軍之集，比當西過，滑臺還為魏有，何必建旗鼓以耀威武乎？

translations.literal: Hezhi said, "The Campaigning King is temporarily staying here to await the gathering of the host; he will presently pass west, and Huatai will again be Wei's—why must you raise banners and display martial might?"
translations.idiomatic: Hezhi said, "The Campaigning King waits here only for the main force. He will soon pass west, and Huatai will be Wei's again—why raise banners to flaunt your might?"

sentences.zh: 」仲德卑辭，常自言不敢與大魏抗衡，建不能制之。

translations.literal: Zhongde used humble words and often said himself he did not dare contend with Great Wei; Jian could not restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongde spoke humbly and often said he would not contend with Great Wei; Jian could not hold him.

sentences.zh: 太宗令建與劉裕相聞，以觀其意。

translations.literal: Taizong ordered Jian to communicate with Liu Yu and observe his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong ordered Jian to sound out Liu Yu and read his intent.

sentences.zh: 裕答言：「洛是晉之舊京，而羌姚據之。

translations.literal: Yu replied, "Luoyang is the old capital of Jin, yet the Qiang Yao hold it.
translations.idiomatic: Yu replied, "Luoyang is Jin's old capital, yet the Qiang of Yao hold it.

sentences.zh: 晉欲修復山陵之計久矣，而內難屢興，不暇經營。

translations.literal: Jin has long wished to restore the imperial tombs, but internal troubles have repeatedly arisen and there was no leisure to undertake it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin has long wished to restore the tombs, but repeated internal troubles left no leisure to act.

sentences.zh: 司馬休之、魯宗之父子、司馬國璠兄弟、諸桓宗屬，皆晉之蠹也，而姚氏收集此等，欲以圖晉，是以伐之。

translations.literal: Sima Xiuzhi, father and son of Lu Zongzhi, the brothers Sima Guofan, and the various Huan clansmen were all pests of Jin, yet the Yao gathered them intending to plot against Jin; therefore we campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiuzhi, Lu Zongzhi and his son, the brothers Sima Guofan, and the Huan kin were pests of Jin; Yao gathered them to plot against Jin, and so we march.

sentences.zh: 道由於魏，軍之初舉，將以重幣假途。

translations.literal: The route passes through Wei; at the army's first setting out, heavy gifts were to be offered to borrow the road.
translations.idiomatic: The route passes through Wei; at the first setting out we meant to offer heavy gifts to borrow the road.

sentences.zh: 會彼邊鎮棄守而去，故晉前軍得以西進，非敢憑陵魏境。

translations.literal: It happened that their border garrison abandoned and left, so the Jin vanguard was able to advance west; it was not that they relied on bullying Wei's territory.
translations.idiomatic: Their border commander abandoned his post, so our vanguard could advance west—we did not mean to bully Wei.

sentences.zh: 」裕以官軍在河南，恐斷其前路，乃命引軍北寇，及班師，乃止。

translations.literal: Yu, because the government army was in Henan, feared his forward route would be cut and therefore ordered the army to raid north; only when they withdrew did it stop. The account is in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing his route would be cut while government troops held Henan, Yu ordered a northern raid; only when they withdrew did it end. The account is in the imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 語在帝紀。

translations.literal: The account is in the imperial annals.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in the imperial annals.

sentences.zh: 建與南平公長孫嵩各簡精兵二千，觀劉裕事勢。

translations.literal: Jian and Zhangsun Song, Duke of Nanping, each picked two thousand elite troops to observe Liu Yu's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Zhangsun Song, Duke of Nanping, each chose two thousand elite troops to watch Liu Yu's movements.

sentences.zh: 語在嵩傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Song's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in Song's biography.

sentences.zh: 遷廣阿鎮將，羣盜斂跡，威名甚震。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison commander of Guang'a; bandits restrained their steps and his renown was greatly feared.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Guang'a, he cowed the bandits and his name carried far.

sentences.zh: 久之，除使持節、都督前鋒諸軍事、楚兵將軍、徐州刺史，率眾自平原濟河，徇下青兗諸郡。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made Bearer of the Staff of Authority, Commander-in-Chief of the Vanguard, General of Chu Troops, and Governor of Xu Province, leading his host across the river from Pingyuan and overrunning the commanderies of Qing and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later given the staff of authority as commander of the vanguard, named General of Chu Troops and Governor of Xu Province, and led his force from Pingyuan across the river through Qing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 建濟河，劉裕兗州刺史徐琰奔彭城，建遂東入青州。

translations.literal: Jian crossed the river; Liu Yu's Governor of Yan Province Xu Yan fled to Pengcheng, and Jian then entered Yan Province in the east.
translations.idiomatic: Jian crossed the river; Xu's Yan fled to Pengcheng, and Jian marched east into Yan Province.

sentences.zh: 司馬受之、秀之先聚黨於濟東，皆率眾降。

translations.literal: Sima Shouzhi and Xiuzhi had earlier gathered factions east of the Ji; both led their hosts to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Shouzhi and Xiuzhi had raised factions east of the Ji; both brought their men over.

sentences.zh: 建入臨淄。

translations.literal: Jian entered Linzi.
translations.idiomatic: Jian entered Linzi.

sentences.zh: 劉義符前東牟太守清河張幸先匿孤山，[4]聞建至，率二千人迎建於女水，遂圍義符青州刺史竺夔於東陽城。

translations.literal: Zhang Xing, former Administrator of Dongmou under Liu Yifu, had earlier hidden on Gushan; hearing Jian had come, he led two thousand men to welcome Jian at the Women's River and then besieged Yifu's Governor of Qing Province Zhu Kui at Dongyang city.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xing, Yifu's former administrator of Dongmou, had hidden on Gushan; when Jian came he led two thousand men to meet him at the Women's River and besieged Zhu Kui at Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 義符遣將檀道濟、王仲德救夔，建不克而還。

translations.literal: Yifu sent the generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde to rescue Kui; Jian could not take the city and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu sent Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde to relieve Kui; Jian could not take the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 建以功賜爵壽光侯，加鎮南將軍。

translations.literal: For merit Jian was granted the title Marquis of Shouguang and additionally named General Who Guards the South.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Marquis of Shouguang and additionally General Who Guards the South.

sentences.zh: 建表曰：「臣前遣沙門僧護詣彭城。

translations.literal: Jian memorialized, "Your servant earlier sent the monk Seng Hu to Pengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Jian memorialized: "Your servant earlier sent the monk Seng Hu to Pengcheng.

sentences.zh: 僧護還稱，賊發軍向北，前鋒將徐卓之已至彭城，大將軍到彥之軍在泗口，發馬戒嚴，必有舉斧之志。

translations.literal: Seng Hu on returning said the enemy had sent troops north; the vanguard general Xu Zhuozhi had already reached Pengcheng, and Grand General Dao Yanzhi's army was at Sikou, issuing horses and proclaiming alert—surely they intend to raise the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Seng Hu reports that the enemy has marched north: the vanguard Xu Zhuozhi is already at Pengcheng, and Grand General Dao Yanzhi is at Sikou, calling up horses and standing to arms—they surely mean to strike."

sentences.zh: 臣聞為國之道，存不忘亡。

translations.literal: Your servant has heard that the way to govern a state is, in security, not to forget peril.
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that the way to govern a state is, in security, never to forget peril.

sentences.zh: 宜繕甲兵，增益屯戍，先為之備，以待其來。

translations.literal: It is fitting to repair armor and weapons, increase garrison troops, prepare beforehand, and await their coming.
translations.idiomatic: We should repair arms, strengthen the garrisons, and prepare in advance for their arrival.

sentences.zh: 若不豫設，卒難擒殄。

translations.literal: If we do not prepare beforehand, in the end they will be hard to capture and destroy.
translations.idiomatic: Without prior preparation, they will be hard to capture and destroy when they come.

sentences.zh: 且吳越之眾，便於舟檝，今至北土，舍其所長。

translations.literal: Moreover the people of Wu and Yue are skilled with boats; coming to the northern lands, they abandon what they excel at.
translations.idiomatic: The men of Wu and Yue excel on the water; in the north they leave that strength behind.

sentences.zh: 逆順既殊，勞逸不等，平寇定功，在於此日。

translations.literal: Right and wrong are already different, toil and rest are unequal—to pacify bandits and fix merit lies in this day.
translations.idiomatic: The odds favor us, their labor tells against them—this is the day to break them and seal our merit.

sentences.zh: 臣雖衰弊，謀略寡淺，過蒙殊寵，忝荷重任，討除寇暴，臣之志也。

translations.literal: Your servant, though declining and feeble, with shallow counsel, has unduly received exceptional favor and bears a heavy charge; to campaign against and remove violent raiders is your servant's aim.
translations.idiomatic: I am old and worn, my counsel shallow, yet I bear a heavy charge beyond my deserts; to drive off the raiders is my aim.

sentences.zh: 是以秣馬枕戈，思效微節。

translations.literal: Therefore he fed horses and slept beside weapons, thinking to repay a small measure of loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: So I have fed my horses and slept beside my weapons, ready to repay what little I can.

sentences.zh: 願陛下不以南境為憂。

translations.literal: I pray Your Majesty will not take the southern frontier to heart.
translations.idiomatic: I pray Your Majesty will not worry over the southern frontier.

sentences.zh: 」世祖優詔答之，賜以衣馬。

translations.literal: Shizu replied with a gracious edict and granted him robes and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu answered with a gracious edict and gave him robes and horses.

sentences.zh: 建與汝陰公長孫道生濟河而南，彥之、仲德等自清入濟，東走青州。

translations.literal: Jian and Zhangsun Daosheng, Duke of Ruyin, crossed the river south; Yanzhi, Zhongde, and others entered the Ji from the Qing and fled east toward Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: Jian and Zhangsun Daosheng, Duke of Ruyin, crossed south; Yanzhi and Zhongde entered the Ji from the Qing and fled east toward Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 劉義隆兗州刺史竺靈秀棄須昌，南奔湖陸，建追擊，大破之，斬首五千餘級，遂至鄒魯。

translations.literal: Liu Yifu's Governor of Yan Province Zhu Lingxiu abandoned Xuchang and fled south to Hulu; Jian pursued, defeated him greatly, took more than five thousand heads, and reached Zou and Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Lingxiu, Yifu's governor of Yan, abandoned Xuchang and fled to Hulu; Jian pursued, broke him, took more than five thousand heads, and reached Zou and Lu.

sentences.zh: 還屯范城。

translations.literal: He returned and encamped at Fancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He withdrew and camped at Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 世祖以建威名南震，為義隆所憚，除平原鎮大將，封丹陽王，加征南大將軍、都督冀青徐濟四州諸軍事。

translations.literal: Shizu, because Jian's martial renown shook the south and Yifu feared him, made him Great General of Pingyuan Garrison, enfeoffed him as Prince of Danyang, and additionally named Great General Who Conquers the South and Commander-in-Chief of military affairs in Ji, Qing, Xu, and Ji provinces.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu made Jian Great General of Pingyuan Garrison and Prince of Danyang, with the additional titles Great General Who Conquers the South and commander of Ji, Qing, Xu, and Ji—Yifu feared his name.

sentences.zh: 先是，簡幽州以南戍兵集于河上，一道討洛陽，一道攻滑臺。

translations.literal: Earlier, frontier troops south of You Province had been selected and gathered on the river; one route was to campaign against Luoyang, another to attack Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, garrison troops south of You had been gathered on the river: one column for Luoyang, one for Huatai.

sentences.zh: 義隆將檀道濟、王仲德救滑臺，建與汝陰公道生拒擊之。

translations.literal: Yifu's generals Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde came to rescue Huatai; Jian and Daosheng, Duke of Ruyin, resisted and struck them.
translations.idiomatic: Tan Daoji and Wang Zhongde came to relieve Huatai; Jian and Daosheng met and fought them.

sentences.zh: 建分軍挾戰，縱輕騎邀其前後，焚燒穀草，以絕其糧道。

translations.literal: Jian divided his army for flank attacks, sent light cavalry to intercept front and rear, and burned grain and fodder to cut their supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Jian split his force for flank attacks, sent light horse to cut front and rear, and burned grain to sever their supply line.

sentences.zh: 道濟兵飢，叛者相繼，由是安頡等得拔滑臺。

translations.literal: Daoji's army went hungry and deserters followed one another; thereby An Gu and others were able to lift the siege of Huatai.
translations.idiomatic: Daoji's men starved and deserters fell away in chains, so An Gu and others could take Huatai.

sentences.zh: 建沉敏多智，東西征伐，常為謀主。

translations.literal: Jian was deep, keen, and full of stratagems; in campaigns east and west he was often the chief planner.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was deep, keen, and full of plans; east and west he was often the mind behind the campaign.

sentences.zh: 治軍清整，號令嚴明。

translations.literal: He governed the army with clarity and order; commands and prohibitions were strict and bright.
translations.idiomatic: He kept his army in clear order; his commands were strict and bright.

sentences.zh: 又雅尚人倫，禮賢愛士。

translations.literal: He also by nature honored human relations and treated the worthy and scholars with ritual and love.
translations.idiomatic: He honored human bonds and treated worthy men and scholars with ritual regard.

sentences.zh: 在平原十餘年，綏懷內外，甚得邊稱，魏初名將尠有及之。

translations.literal: For more than ten years at Pingyuan he soothed within and without and won great praise on the frontier; among the famed generals of early Wei few could match him.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years at Pingyuan he soothed within and without and won high praise on the frontier; few generals of early Wei could match him.

sentences.zh: 南方憚其威略，青兗輒不為寇。

translations.literal: The south feared his martial designs, and Qing and Yan were seldom troubled by raiders.
translations.idiomatic: The south feared his designs, and Qing and Yan were seldom raided.

sentences.zh: 太延三年薨，時年七十三。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiyan he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taiyan, at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 世祖悼惜之。

translations.literal: Shizu mourned and regretted him.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu mourned him deeply.

sentences.zh: 諡曰襄王，賜葬金陵。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Prince Xiang and granted burial at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Prince Xiang and buried by accompaniment at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 長子俊，字醜歸，少聰敏。

translations.literal: His eldest son Jun, styled Chougui, was clever and keen in youth.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Jun, styled Chougui, was clever as a boy.

sentences.zh: 年十五，內侍左右。

translations.literal: At fifteen he attended within the palace at the ruler's side.
translations.idiomatic: At fifteen he attended within the palace.

sentences.zh: 性謹密，初無過行。

translations.literal: His nature was careful and close; at first he had no misdeeds.
translations.idiomatic: He was careful and discreet and at first without fault.

sentences.zh: 以便弓馬，轉為獵郎。

translations.literal: Because he was skilled with bow and horse, he was transferred to be a hunt attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Skilled with bow and horse, he was made a hunt attendant.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，清河王紹閉宮門，太宗在外。

translations.literal: When Taizu died, Prince Qinghe Shao closed the palace gates while Taizong was outside.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu died, Prince Qinghe Shao shut the palace gates while Taizong was outside.

sentences.zh: 紹逼俊以為己援。

translations.literal: Shao forced Jun to be his supporter.
translations.idiomatic: Shao pressed Jun to back him.

sentences.zh: 俊外雖從紹，內實忠款，仍與元磨渾等說紹，得歸太宗。

translations.literal: Outwardly Jun followed Shao, but inwardly he was truly loyal; together with Yuan Mohun and others he persuaded Shao and was able to return to Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he followed Shao, but inwardly he stayed loyal; with Yuan Mohun and others he turned Shao and returned to Taizong.

sentences.zh: 事在磨渾傳。

translations.literal: The account is in Mohun's biography.
translations.idiomatic: The full account is in Mohun's biography.

sentences.zh: 是時太宗左右，唯車路頭、王洛兒等，及得俊等，大悅，以為爪牙。

translations.literal: At that time at Taizong's side were only Chelu Tou, Wang Luo'er, and others; when he gained Jun and the rest he was greatly pleased and took them as claws and fangs.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then had only Chelu Tou, Wang Luo'er, and a few others at his side; when he gained Jun he was overjoyed and made them his claws and fangs.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，命俊與磨渾等拾遺左右。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he ordered Jun with Mohun and others to remedy omissions at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong came to the throne, he set Jun with Mohun and others to remedy omissions at his side.

sentences.zh: 遷衞將軍，賜爵安城公。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General of the Guards and granted the title Duke of Ancheng.
translations.idiomatic: He was made General of the Guards and Duke of Ancheng.

sentences.zh: 朱提王悅懷刃入禁中，將為大逆。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhuti Yue, with a blade hidden, entered the forbidden precinct intending great treason.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhuti Yue entered the inner palace with a hidden blade, intent on treason.

sentences.zh: 俊覺悅舉動有異，便引手掣之，乃於悅懷中得兩刃匕首，遂殺之。

translations.literal: Jun noticed Yue's movements were strange, reached out and seized him, and from Yue's bosom obtained two-bladed daggers; he then killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jun saw Yue's manner was strange, seized him, and found twin daggers in his bosom; he killed him on the spot.

sentences.zh: 太宗以俊前後功重，軍國大計一以委之，群官上事，先由俊銓校，然後奏聞。

translations.literal: Taizong, because Jun's merits before and after were weighty, entrusted all great plans of army and state to him; officials' memorials first passed through Jun's review and then were submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong entrusted army and state to Jun for his repeated service; memorials passed through Jun's review before they reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 性平正柔和，未嘗有喜怒之色。

translations.literal: His nature was even, upright, gentle, and mild; he never showed the color of anger or joy.
translations.idiomatic: He was even, upright, gentle, and mild and never showed anger or joy on his face.

sentences.zh: 忠篤愛厚，不諂上抑下。

translations.literal: Loyal, sincere, loving, and generous, he did not flatter those above or suppress those below.
translations.idiomatic: He was loyal, sincere, and generous and neither flattered his superiors nor pressed his inferiors.

sentences.zh: 每奉詔宣外，必告示殷勤，受事者皆飽之而退，事密者倍至蒸仍。

translations.literal: Whenever he bore edicts abroad he always announced them with earnest care; those who received his charge left satisfied, and for secret matters he redoubled his warmth.
translations.idiomatic: When he carried edicts abroad he announced them with earnest care; those who received his charge left satisfied, and secret matters won redoubled warmth.

sentences.zh: 是以上下嘉歎。

translations.literal: Therefore above and below praised and sighed.
translations.idiomatic: High and low praised him.

sentences.zh: 泰常元年卒，時年二十八，太宗甚痛悼之，親臨哀慟。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taichang he died, aged twenty-eight; Taizong mourned him deeply and came in person to weep.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Taichang, at twenty-eight; Taizong mourned in person.

sentences.zh: 朝野無不追惜。

translations.literal: At court and in the countryside none failed to mourn and regret him.
translations.idiomatic: Court and countryside mourned him.

sentences.zh: 贈侍中、司空、安城王，諡孝元。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, and the title Prince of Ancheng, with the posthumous name Xiaoyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously named Attendant-in-Ordinary, Minister of Works, Prince of Ancheng, with the posthumous title Xiaoyuan.

sentences.zh: 賜溫明祕器，載以轀輬車，衞士導從，陪葬金陵。

translations.literal: He was granted the secret coffin of Wenming, carried on the imperial hearse, with guards as escort, and buried by accompaniment at Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the secret coffin of Wenming, carried on the imperial hearse with guards as escort, and buried by accompaniment at Jinling.

sentences.zh: 子蒲，襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Pu inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Pu inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 後有大功及寵幸貴臣薨，賻送終禮，皆依俊故事，無得踰之者。

translations.literal: Later, when great ministers of merit or favored officials died, the gifts and funeral rites all followed Jun's precedent and none might exceed it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when great ministers or favored officials died, funeral gifts followed Jun's precedent and none might exceed it.

sentences.zh: 初，俊既卒，太宗命其妻桓氏曰：「夫生既共榮，沒宜同穴，能殉葬者可任意。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Jun had died, Taizong told his wife Lady Huan, "In life you shared glory together; in death you should share one tomb. Whoever is willing to follow in burial may do as she wishes."
translations.idiomatic: When Jun died, Taizong told his wife Lady Huan: "In life you shared glory; in death you should share one tomb. Whoever will follow in burial may do so."

sentences.zh: 」桓氏乃縊而死，遂合葬焉。

translations.literal: Lady Huan then hanged herself and was buried together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Huan hanged herself and was buried with him.

sentences.zh: 俊既為安城王，俊弟隣襲公爵，降為丹陽公。

translations.literal: Since Jun had become Prince of Ancheng, his younger brother Lin inherited the ducal title and was reduced to Duke of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun became Prince of Ancheng, his younger brother Lin inherited the ducal title and was reduced to Duke of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 少聰慧知名。

translations.literal: In youth he was clever and famed.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he was clever and well known.

sentences.zh: 稍遷北部尚書，有當官之稱。

translations.literal: He was gradually advanced to Minister of the Northern Bureau and had the reputation of fulfilling his office.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Minister of the Northern Bureau and won a name for fulfilling his office.

sentences.zh: 轉尚書令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 出為涼州鎮大將，加鎮西將軍。

translations.literal: He was sent out as Great General of Liang Province Garrison and additionally named General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as Great General of Liang Province Garrison and additionally General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 隣與鎮副將奚牧，並以貴戚子弟，競貪財貨，專作威福。

translations.literal: Lin and the deputy garrison commander Xi Mu, both sons of noble consort kin, vied in greed for wealth and goods and monopolized power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and the deputy commander Xi Mu, both noble kinsmen, vied in greed and abused their power.

sentences.zh: 遂相糾發，坐伏誅。

translations.literal: They then denounced each other and were both executed for their crimes.
translations.idiomatic: They denounced each other and were both executed.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：奚斤世稱忠孝，征伐有克。

translations.literal: The historian says: Xi Jin for generations was called loyal and filial; in campaigns he had successes.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: Xi Jin's line was called loyal and filial, and in the field he won his share.

sentences.zh: 平涼之役，師殲身虜。

translations.literal: In the Pingliang campaign the army was destroyed and he was taken captive.
translations.idiomatic: At Pingliang his army was destroyed and he was taken captive.

sentences.zh: 雖敗崤之責已赦，封尸之效靡立，而恩禮隆渥，沒祀廟庭。

translations.literal: Though the blame of defeat at Yao was already pardoned and the effect of sealing the corpses was not established, favor and ritual were thick and generous and after death he was sacrificed in the temple court.
translations.idiomatic: Though the blame for Yao was pardoned and he never sealed the enemy dead on the field, favor and ritual were lavish and he was honored in the temple after death.

sentences.zh: 叔孫建少展誠勤，終著庸伐。

translations.literal: Shu Sun Jian in youth showed sincere diligence and in the end achieved meritorious campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Shu Sun Jian showed sincere diligence in youth and meritorious service in the end.

sentences.zh: 治邊有術，威震夷楚。

translations.literal: Governing the frontier he had method; his might shook the Yi and Chu.
translations.idiomatic: He governed the frontier with method; his might shook the south.

sentences.zh: 俊委節太宗，義彰顛沛，察朱提之變，有日磾之風。

translations.literal: Jun entrusted his integrity to Taizong and righteousness shone in hardship; detecting the change of Zhu Ti, he had the wind of Jin Midi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun gave his integrity to Taizong in hardship; sensing Zhu Ti's plot, he had the spirit of Jin Midi.

sentences.zh: 加以柔而有正，見美朝野，可謂世不乏賢矣。

translations.literal: Added to this, gentle yet upright, he was praised at court and in the countryside; one may say the age did not lack worthy men.
translations.idiomatic: Gentle yet upright, praised at court and in the countryside—his age did not lack worthy men.
